https://www.printweek.in/article/aarya-p.text: Share article on Twitter Share article on Facebook Share article on LinkedIn Sameer Popli with his Bindwel 6 Clamp Perfect Binder Aayra Production operates from an 18,000 sqft factory in Sonipat, Haryana, employing approximately 70 staff members. Promoted by founder Sameer Popli, the business has engaged in book printing and bookbinding for over 35 years. The facility houses pre-press, press, and post-press operations under one roof. The printing department consists of two Heidelberg four-colour presses, one Heidelberg two-colour press, and a paper cutting machine. The post-press section includes a Brehmer folding machine, a 24-station Polygraph gathering machine, five Polygraph section sewing machines, a Muller Martini Amigo perfect binder, a Wohlenberg three-knife trimmer, and a Bindwel 6 Clamp Perfect Binder installed two years ago. The plant processes Maplitho paper, coated paper, and publishing paper substrates ranging from 52 gsm to 120 gsm. Its product portfolio encompasses educational books, commercial books, perfect binding, hard case binding, wire binding, and passport binding. “Prior to the installation of the Bindwel system, operations were affected by machine breakdowns, downtime, dependence on local mechanics, and limited spare-part availability for ageing imported equipment,” informed Popli adding further, “Aayra Production selected the Bindwel 6 Clamp Perfect Binder based on its domestic manufacturing source, spare-part availability, and technical support access. The machine features a touchscreen interface and Adhesive Coating Control (ECC) technology.” He notes that since the installation, the facility records an output of approximately 18,000 books per 12-hour shift, alongside lower adhesive consumption achieved through the ECC system. “The machine has also reduced book and cover wastage, while technical issues are addressed through phone support and engineer visits within hours,” added Popli. The integrated workflow was utilised for an export order comprising 1,00,000 books sent to Poland. “The project recorded near-zero quality rejections during final dispatch inspection!” Popli informed. Commenting on broader industry shifts, the founder noted that increasing labour costs, higher operating expenses, and rising infrastructure costs are driving printing and binding facilities towards higher automation and factory space consolidation. Aayra Production plans to add further automated binding machinery over the next five to 10 years.
